translationRepairs: In 1354 the court appointed Yu Hanlin attendant compiler and Gentleman for Discussion, sent envoys bearing imperial wine and famous silks, and summoned him by sea.
In 1354 the court appointed Yu as Hanlin attendant compiler and Gentleman for Discussion, sent envoys bearing imperial wine and famous silks, and summoned him by sea.

s0075 朝廷除玉翰林待制、奉議大夫 appoints 玉 to the offices 翰林待制 and 奉議大夫; without "as," "Yu Hanlin" can be misread as a fused personal name, so the proposed wording correctly separates the person from the Hanlin title.
In 1357, when Ming forces entered Huizhou, the defending commander was about to hand him over. Yu said, "Would I serve two dynasties!"
In 1357, when Ming forces entered Huizhou, the defending commander was about to bring him over. Yu said, "Would I serve two dynasties!"

s0080 守將將要致之, followed by 吾豈事二姓者耶, means the commander sought to bring Yu over into Ming service, not hand him over as a captive; "bring him over" matches 致之 and the refusal to serve two dynasties, and s0081 因被拘囚 follows that refusal.
